QF.id: Registration, Code of Conduct and General Obligations_26

question.text: Under the Code of Conduct (Schedule III), what is the percentage shareholding threshold in the issuer company beyond which key personnel of a merchant banker are prohibited from managing the public issue?

answer.text: More than 1% of the issuer's shares
More than 0.5% of the issuer's shares
More than 5% of the issuer's shares
More than 0.1% of the issuer's shares

explanation.text: The Logic: Schedule III specifies that a merchant banker cannot manage a public issue if its key personnel hold more than the lower of 0.1% of paid-up share capital or shares with nominal value above Rs. 10 lakh. In percentage terms, the threshold called out by this question is 0.1% of paid-up share capital. The Trap: The 1% threshold is associated with other SEBI disclosure rules and is not the Schedule III conflict-of-interest threshold for managing the issue. Other percentages in the options are not the Schedule III figure. Note: The full rule has two prongs - the percentage threshold (0.1%) and a nominal-value alternative (above Rs. 10 lakh), whichever is lower; a marketing-only appointment may be permitted subject to disclosures. This question is scoped to the percentage threshold only.
